sources.name: ExRx (Kilgore/Rippetoe, ages 18-39)
sources.population: adult (18-39) trained recreational lifters; levels derived from historical weightlifting/powerlifting classification systems
sources.notes: 1RM, paused touch, no supportive gear. Male table seen in full in one snippet and matches the widely quoted Kilgore table. Female rows assembled from 3 snippets; Untrained/Novice for 148/165/181 not seen (null). Female 199+ row: Untrained 95, Novice 120 (others not seen). Top ExRx class is 319 lb (men) / 199+ lb (women); app's 310 lb maps to 319.

sources.name: StrengthLog (app users)
sources.population: StrengthLog workout-app users: training logs of 17,296 men and 7,112 women (self-logged gym-goers)
sources.mapping: Beginner->Beginner (5th pct), Novice->Novice (25th pct; SL uses 20th), Intermediate->Intermediate (50th), Advanced->Advanced (75th pct; SL uses 80th), Elite->Elite (95th)
sources.notes: 1RM in lb from the site's lb tables (10-lb steps). Page ~2.5 years old. Novice/Advanced percentiles are 25/75 (not 20/80 as in Strength Level), so Novice should read slightly higher and Advanced slightly lower than SL even on identical data.

Bench Press.summary: SL re-check matches the app exactly. Versus SL, ExRx men are higher at Beginner/Novice for light lifters, about equal at 180 lb Int (200 vs 220), but far lower for heavy men (319 lb Elite 415 vs SL 310 lb 497; Int 245 vs 351). StrengthLog runs ~5-15% below SL at Intermediate-Elite for men (200 lb: 225/272/350 vs 243/303/367) and ~20-30% lower at 110 lb; for women StrengthLog is higher at Beginner/Novice and lower at Intermediate+ (120 lb Int 89 vs 95, Adv 107 vs 137).

Incline Bench Press.summary: SL female light/heavy rows match the app exactly. No other gym-goer per-body-weight table found for this lift (ExRx/StrengthLog only cover flat bench and overhead press; FitnessVolt tables are derived from competition data and were excluded).

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: none (male 110 also re-seen: Beginner 56, Elite 232 - matches)

Decline Bench Press.summary: SL male heavy rows match the app exactly. No other gym-goer per-body-weight table found for this lift (ExRx/StrengthLog only cover flat bench and overhead press; FitnessVolt tables are derived from competition data and were excluded).

Dumbbell Bench Press.summary: SL rows (per dumbbell) match the app exactly. No other gym-goer per-body-weight table found for this lift (ExRx/StrengthLog only cover flat bench and overhead press; FitnessVolt tables are derived from competition data and were excluded).

Incline Dumbbell Bench Press.summary: SL extreme rows (per dumbbell) match the app exactly. No other gym-goer per-body-weight table found for this lift (ExRx/StrengthLog only cover flat bench and overhead press; FitnessVolt tables are derived from competition data and were excluded).

Close Grip Bench Press.summary: SL rows match the app exactly, including the male 260/310 rows the app had at confidence 2. No other gym-goer per-body-weight table found for this lift (ExRx/StrengthLog only cover flat bench and overhead press; FitnessVolt tables are derived from competition data and were excluded).

sources.name: ExRx (Kilgore/Rippetoe Press, ages 18-39)
sources.population: adult (18-39) trained recreational lifters; standing strict barbell press
sources.notes: Strict standing barbell press (knees straight, no layback), 1RM. Rows from snippets that were summarised, not full tables; 165 row was 'roughly'. One snippet gave a 198-lb row of 55/75/85/115/150 which conflicts with neighbours (likely an older-age table) and is NOT recorded. Female '199' = ExRx '199+' class. App 'Shoulder Press' may include seated/standing; ExRx is standing strict.

sources.name: StrengthLog (app users)
sources.population: StrengthLog workout-app users: 14,081 men and 5,711 women (self-logged gym-goers)
sources.mapping: Beginner->Beginner (5th pct), Novice->Novice (25th pct; SL uses 20th), Intermediate->Intermediate (50th), Advanced->Advanced (75th pct; SL uses 80th), Elite->Elite (95th)
sources.notes: Barbell overhead press (no leg drive), 1RM. Page ~3.5 years old. One summary claimed the men's lb table has an odd drop between 160 and 170 lb rows (Int 109 -> 68); 170 row not recorded. Percentiles 5/25/50/75/95 vs SL 5/20/50/80/95.

Shoulder Press.summary: SL re-check matches the app exactly. ExRx men agree closely with SL around 180 lb (80/110/140/165/220 vs 75/104/140/181/226) but are lower at heavy body weights (275 lb Int 165 vs SL ~193). StrengthLog is notably lower than SL above Novice (180 lb: Int 120 vs 140, Adv 140 vs 181, Elite 177 vs 226, i.e. ~15-22% lower); for women both alternates are higher than SL at Beginner/Novice and lower at Advanced/Elite.

Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press.summary: SL rows (per dumbbell) match the app exactly, so the app's confidence-2 rows can be upgraded. No other gym-goer per-body-weight table found for this lift (ExRx/StrengthLog only cover flat bench and overhead press; FitnessVolt tables are derived from competition data and were excluded).

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: none (SL shows '<1' where the app stores 0)

Dips.summary: SL rows match the app exactly. No other per-body-weight dip-rep standard found (ExRx/StrengthLog have none).

strength_level_check.differs_from_app: Seen rows match. App is MISSING female 200 and 220-260; a snippet (sex not labelled, but values fit the female table, male 260 Elite is 67) gave Elite only: 220->34, 230->33, 240->32, 250->31, 260->30. Other levels for those rows not seen.

Push Ups.summary: SL rows match the app; female rows 200 and 220-260 are still missing from the app (only Elite values 34..30 seen for 220-260). Only other push-up norms found are age-based fitness-test tables (YMCA/ACSM style, no body-weight dimension, unverified attribution), so not usable as a per-body-weight source.
